issues.description: Confusing boolean logic: `not X and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is hard to read and wrong-shaped
issues.detail: The condition reads `not self.get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab`. Two `not`s with a comparison hiding in the middle, no parens. `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` should be `key != Qt.Key_Tab`. Better yet, invert and split: cache the config value, then `if key == Qt.Key_Tab: fall through; elif not accept_with_enter: hide and forward`. The maintainer six years from now will misread this.

issues.description: get_conf called on every keyPressEvent — config read in the hot path
issues.detail: The new check sits inside keyPressEvent, which fires for every keystroke while the completion widget is up. Reading config through get_conf on every key is wasteful and couples the keypress handler to the config system's performance. Cache the value on the widget and update it via a config-change signal, or at minimum read it inside the narrower branch instead of unconditionally.

issues.description: New check placed before the existing `item is None` guard, tangling control flow
issues.detail: The new block runs before `if item is None: item = self.item(0)`. It works through the negation, but the logic is tangled with the surrounding item lookup. Lift the new block to a clearly-commented early branch (Enter/Return path when option is off) rather than wedging it ahead of unrelated guard code.

issues.description: Diff doesn't match surrounding style — multi-line get_conf call is awkwardly wrapped
issues.detail: The surrounding file uses fairly compact conditionals. The new three-line `if not self.get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab:` reads poorly. A local `accept_with_enter = self.get_conf(...)` above the conditional would match the codebase voice and shorten the if.

issues.description: No test coverage in the diff for the new behavior
issues.detail: A new user-facing option that changes a keypress code path lands with zero tests. Spyder has editor/completion tests; this needed at least one — option off, press Enter, assert completion did not insert and the Enter was forwarded to the editor. Otherwise this regresses silently the first time someone refactors keyPressEvent.

issues.description: PR description explains what, not why
issues.detail: "Add option to disable enter in completions" — fine as a subject, but the description repeats it verbatim. Why does this option exist? Vim users, people whose muscle memory hits Enter to insert a newline, etc. Why-not-what, useful forever in git blame.
The section name is hardcoded in the new get_conf call. If a constant exists for it elsewhere in the completions plugin, use it. Minor.

review.summary: The patch does one thing — adds a config option to disable Enter as a completion-accept key — and that's good. The shape is right and it's small. But the keyPressEvent change has bad taste: a double-negative conditional with a comparison hiding inside `not key == Qt.Key_Tab`, plus a config read on every keystroke. Both are fixable with a cached value and a clearer if/else. No tests, and the PR description explains what instead of why. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — fix the conditional, cache the config value, add one test, rewrite the description. Then it lands.
